messages:
maria: heads up — helm upgrade of gpupool chart in eu-west canary failed and stuck the canary job. post-upgrade hook errors out with a conversion webhook 429. this is blocking gpupool from scaling.
connor: oh no. do you have the hook logs?
maria: pasted below — it's the conversion webhook call getting throttled by the control plane
```
I0312 10:14:22.123456 1 request.go:123] POST /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions: 429 Too Many Requests
E0312 10:14:22.124000 1 webhook.go:98] conversion webhook returned 429, patch aborted
```
ashley: that rate limit makes sense, we pushed a large gitops rollout ~9:30 that reconciled dozens of CRDs across regions. looks like the conversion webhook is stateful and the canary keeps retrying.
raj: fwiw, the canary's post-upgrade job calls a metadata service in a loop (terraform change last week) — that spike probably amplified calls to the apiserver. i'm patching the job to reduce retries.
connor: does this actually affect GPU capacity? we saw a customer report fail to allocate a pod to gpupool after scale attempt.
maria: yes — autoscaler is waiting on gpupool CR update; because canary hook never finishes the gpupool controller won't mark nodes as ready for allocation. customers fell back to on-demand nodes, increasing cost ~30% for that cluster window.
sre-oncall: confirmed oncall alert matching this — API server throttling correlated with mass CR updates and webhook hits. cloud provider also returned a few 503s around the same time.
ashley: short-term mitigation: 1) delete the canary hook job to let previous gpupool controller reconcile (manual cleanup), 2) patch the helm release to skip hooks for canary (helm upgrade --set canary.hooks=false), 3) backoff job retries. longer-term: make conversion webhook horizontally scalable or add client-side rate limiting.
maria: i've run `kubectl delete job gpupool-canary-posthook -n infra` and restarted gpupool controller. pods are getting scheduled again.
connor: nice. can we avoid this in future helm rollouts? maybe gate canary hooks behind a controller check
raj: opening PR to make the post-upgrade job idempotent + exponential backoff and remove noisy metadata polling. also adding alert that ties gpupool canary hook failures to gpupool-scaling SLO.
sre-oncall: i'm going to raise an incident with cloud support to get API rate limit increased for the control-plane service account used by our gitops controllers. also adding a short term admission webhook rate limiter config so that webhooks return 429 less aggressively (client-retry aware).
deploy-bot: CI pipeline aborted for release 2026.03.12-175 with status: cancelled. linked issue: #INFRA-4821
maria: plan: confirm gpupool is healthy for the region by EOD, merge raj's PR tomorrow, schedule a staged canary with throttling window (small batches), and follow up with cloud for rate limit increase. tagging @connor and @ashley to own rollout guard changes. :thumbsup:
